cases.question: What is the weather forecast for Los Angeles for the next two days?

checkpoints.description: finds a station near Los Angeles on a global forecast network, by name or by point
reads the forecast values of a Los Angeles station, air temperature among them

forbidden.description: refuses, or says no forecast is available, for a place the global forecast network serves
forbidden.regex: (?i)(not eligible|only (covers|provides|for|available for) (germany|german)|german (weather )?(service|provider)[^.]{0,40}(only|cannot)|cannot[^.]{0,40}outside (of )?germany|(cannot|can.t|unable to|no way to) (give|provide|get|offer|find|retrieve|produce|make)[^.]{0,30}forecast|(tools|server|provider)[^.]{0,30}(do not|don.t|does not|doesn.t) (offer|provide|have)[^.]{0,30}forecast|no forecast (data )?(is |was )?(available|offered|found))

forbidden.description: uses interpolate or summarize for a plain question about a named place
asks for shape=wide over a window of more than 3 days, or without a window (overflows the client)
calls values more than twice with the same arguments

facts.description: the answer is about a station in the Los Angeles area

every air temperature the answer gives belongs to a forecast hour (a timestamp after the subject's call) and lies within the span of the forecast the judge reads itself, plus a margin: forecasts change between runs, so never a fixed number, and an observation does not count

ground_truth.pick: all air temperatures of the next 48 hours

cases.notes: Seen on 2026-10-28: a model refused because dwd/mosmix is a German provider (GH-3456), and a Haiku run read observations of nws/observation and said it could not give a forecast. Station 72295 is KLAX; a name search also returns unrelated 'LOS ...' stations, so the first hit must be checked.

cases.question: Which weather data providers have data for Brazil?

checkpoints.description: looks at what the providers are (providers or coverage)
probes a global network for stations near a Brazilian place (there is no country filter); reading the `extent` of the providers is the other valid path, and then this checkpoint is the one missed

forbidden.description: concludes that no provider has data for Brazil
forbidden.regex: (?i)(no provider (has|offers|covers|serves)|none of the providers (has|have|covers?|serves?)|(not|n.t) (available|covered) (for|in) brazil|no (weather )?data (for|in) brazil)

forbidden.description: calls stations more than twice with the same arguments

facts.description: the answer names at least one network that serves Brazil: DWD mosmix or dmo, or NOAA ghcn
the judge probes a network the answer names itself and finds a station within 150 km of Sao Paulo, so the claim is true

ground_truth.pick: the distance of the nearest station, in km (the judge repeats it for the network the answer names, when that is not dwd/mosmix)

cases.notes: No endpoint filters providers by country: the answer is a probe of the global networks (dwd/mosmix, dwd/dmo, noaa/ghcn) and of meteofrance (overseas territories border Brazil), or a reading of the `extent` of each provider. A national network of another continent does not serve Brazil.

facts.description: gives the credit line the judge reads from the providers answer, and says it is the credit line

ground_truth.pick: the attribution (credit line) of dwd, not the copyright line

cases.notes: Two credit strings come with every answer: the attribution ('Source: Deutscher Wetterdienst') and the copyright of the network ('© Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), Climate Data Center (CDC)'). The attribution is the credit line; an answer that gives both and says which is which passes. Ground truth is read from the judge's own call, so a provider listing that moves or compacts these fields does not break the case.

cases.question: Is there any official weather warning active right now for the city of Kiel? If so, which event and how severe?

checkpoints.description: reads the current warnings (either granularity; an absent argument is its default)

forbidden.description: calls alerts more than twice with the same arguments
fetches observations for a warnings question

facts.description: the answer agrees with the warnings of the snapshot the subject itself read: the judge calls alerts again with the subject's arguments and `timestamp` set to the `data_updated_at` of the subject's result, so that both read the same snapshot; the answer names the event of every warning whose area_names contain Kiel, or says there is none when there is none

cases.notes: alerts returns every warning of Germany, each with its full GeoJSON geometry, which can overflow a client's token limit when many are active: a model that has to filter by area_names depends on the answer fitting.
